newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stocks end weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: South African stocks end weaker but off lows.

text.p: South African shares ended weaker but off earlier lows, weighed by worries over the rand's recent slide, dealers said.
Institutional buying offered some support before close after profit-taking hit the market through most of the day. Gold shares ended soft on the back of a dull bullion price.
The rand ended at 4.5010/5040, a whisker lower than Monday's late price of 4.5000/5030.
The industrial index was last down 17.8 points at 8,501.4 points, the gold index was off 4.2 points to 1,777.1 points and the all-share index fell 31.0 points to 7,265.5 points.
Dealers said volumes traded were high at 837 million rand worth of shares.

Dealers said the April all-commodities producer price index which came in at 8.8 percent year-on-year after March's 9.6 percent rise was shrugged off by the market as it was largely in line with expectations.
They said it reinforced hopes of an interest rate cut later this year.
Declining issues led advancers in the broader market by 221 to 174.
There were 27 new highs and 17 new lows.
Dealers said underlying sentiment remained positive as in the last week when the market surged following a suprise peak in the official May reserves.
But fears of capital flight after the easing of some forex controls on July clouded it.
Other dealers said Tuesday's trade levels could be indicating the start of a period of consolidation in the market following its recent strength.
The dealers said some volatility was expected later this week as futures players started to unwind their baskets ahead of next week's futures close-out.
